page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and software compilation speeds fall within the average tier. However, memory subsystem benchmarks reveal a performance tradeoff; while small-block cached read bandwidth is average, large-block uncached read and write bandwidth tests show weaker performance, placing in the bottom 25%. Similarly, Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations register in the lower performance tier.

Given its high memory density relative to compute resources, the ecs.r7a.2xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring substantial memory footprints without demanding extreme memory bandwidth or local storage. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications such as caching layers, medium-sized databases, enterprise applications, and general-purpose web serving.

Utilizing the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 server provides a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, while multi-core processing, software compilation, and static web serving remain in the average tier. A notable tradeoff is observed in memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks and database operations, which perform in the lower 25% tier. With a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy workloads that do not require high-throughput local storage. It is best suited for memory-intensive applications, caching layers, and standard database deployments.
